title: Tamsin and the Compass
premise: In 1794, Tamsin Sebastian, a woman passing as a male courier named Sebastian Winterbourne, carries coded dispatches for a collapsing republic's final diplomatic mission. When one sealed letter implicates her own hidden family in a treason plot, she realizes her invisibility has been someone else's design all along. As evacuation ships prepare to sail and agents close in, she must decide which of her kin takes the last berth — knowing that choosing one means abandoning the others. In the end she gives up her own place, sends her sister aboard with the codes that could save what remains, and stays behind to face the consequences, finding an unexpected belonging among those left on the dock.
about_author: Hazel Villalobos is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing letters from displaced families before turning to fiction. She writes historical novels about people history tried to forget.

chapters.title: The Weight of Sealed Things
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Working as courier 'Sebastian Winterbourne' aboard a diplomatic packet bound for a besieged port city, Tamsin keeps her head down and her hands busy until a sealed letter entrusted to her bears her family's true name inside a treason accusation. The emotional beat is dread disguised as routine — the moment invisibility begins to crack.

chapters.title: What the Codes Confess
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. Deciphering the letter against her duty, she learns the plot is real and that evacuation berths are being quietly traded among officials. Her brother is already compromised; her sister begs her to stay silent. Torn between love and duty, she copies the codes as insurance. The beat is rising tension: every choice now costs something.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. At the harbor, with agents closing in and only one berth left, Tamsin confronts her handler and discovers he has known her identity since the first mile — she was bait all along. Climax: she forces the choice into the open, names her sister for the berth, and burns the letter rather than let it condemn anyone.

chapters.title: Those Who Remain
chapters.summary: POV: Tamsin. The ship sails without her; her sister carries the codes toward safety while Tamsin surrenders to the authorities, expecting ruin but finding instead a community of the left-behind who claim her as their own. Resolution: belonging was never escape — it was staying. Quiet, bittersweet hope closes the book.
